shared_elements: carved stone surface in low relief
circular disc motif (rosettes in A, ring/disc in B)
incised linear detailing over a plain stone ground
justification: Both are stone carvings whose surfaces combine human figural forms, incised linear detail and round disc motifs organised against horizontal bands, which is the most specific correspondence I can point to. But A is a shallow, finely modelled horizontal frieze reading as a left-to-right procession within rosette borders, whereas B is a coarse, weathered free-standing monolith whose few motifs are stacked vertically on a body-shaped block, so composition, scale and carving manner diverge almost entirely.
